rows.grounds: object of the imperative; refers to the supreme nectar mentioned in context
compound in apposition to amṛtaṃ, qualifying it as the true essence of Kaula
compound adjective qualifying kaulasadbhāvaṃ/amṛtaṃ as consisting of Kāmakalā

items.question: How is the nectar identified as the true essence of Kaula characterized?
premises: The nectar is identified as the true essence of Kaula.
This Kaula essence is described as having the nature of Kāmakalā.
The listener is directly instructed to hear about this nectar.
items.inference: The supreme nectar, as the true essence of Kaula, is fundamentally constituted by Kāmakalā.
uncertainties: The precise doctrinal sense of kāmakalā in this context is not fully specified by the verse alone.
items.plain_english: Hear of the nectar, the true essence of Kaula, whose very nature is Kāmakalā.
